answer: In a market for mapping data, agents that wander a canyon must lock $100 for 30 days to earn capacity to sell one sensor pulse per hour. Capacity scales with locked funds, so splitting $100 across a thousand identities earns no extra throughput. An attacker seeking a thousand times the capacity must lock $100,000 for the same month, tying up capital and forgoing its use elsewhere; fresh names alone buy nothing.
